Deciding with the full picture

Anyone selling, buying or renovating a property decides about a lot of money, often on the basis of documents that each show only one side. GRENFORD puts the information side by side before the decision is made.

The idea behind GRENFORD↓The business idea ↓

The idea behind GRENFORD

Why GRENFORD was founded and what sets it apart from a conventional estate agent.

The problem

Sales particulars are meant to sell, contractor quotes are meant to win the job, key figures stand without context. Whoever has to decide receives plenty of documents but rarely the full picture.

The answer

GRENFORD prepares every decision in writing: in the Investment Memo, the Property Brief or the Renovation Memo. Figures, options and open points stand side by side, including those that argue against a quick deal.

The difference

GRENFORD is also paid on completion. But before anything is signed, there is a basis you can review, pass on and discuss with your bank, family or tax adviser. The decision remains yours.

The business idea

Marco Kaimann, founder of GRENFORD

GRENFORD is set up so that every property decision gets a written basis, right where it is made. Each area works on its own, but their real strength shows in how they work together.

Three business areas form the foundation: Investment for the sale and acquisition of investment properties, with the Investment Memo; Property for flats and houses, with the Property Brief; and Projects for renovations, with the Renovation Memo, which makes contractor quotes comparable. The Valuation connects all three: it shows the value today and after a renovation.

The real idea lies in the connection. Depending on the project, the building blocks work together: in a fix-and-flip deal, the Valuation, Renovation Memo and Property Brief together give you the purchase value, renovation costs and achievable sale price. An investment property in need of renovation is underpinned by the Investment Memo and Renovation Memo with reliable quotes instead of estimates. And anyone selling an inherited flat can see from the Valuation and Property Brief whether a refresh before the sale pays off.

Throughout, you have one point of contact. Marco Kaimann handles every mandate personally, drawing on experience at a major Berlin brokerage, in real estate market data and in transactions for private and institutional investors. Where specialist knowledge is required, GRENFORD brings in experts, architects and lenders.

The GRENFORD 5-Point Process

Every mandate follows the same sequence. You decide how much of it you need.

  1. 01

    Understand

    Getting to know your project, your wishes and your goals.

    You receiveAn initial conversation, free of charge

  2. 02

    Assess

    Bringing together framework, documents and options.

    You receiveA first assessment and a list of missing documents

  3. 03

    Analyse

    Making information and differences easy to understand.

    You receiveYour memo: Investment Memo, Property Brief or Renovation Memo

  4. 04

    Decide

    Setting a well-founded direction and the next steps.

    You receiveYour decision, recorded in writing

  5. 05

    Accompany

    Up to the notary appointment or completion of works, within the agreed scope.

    You receiveOne point of contact until completion
